title: Employee Scheduling Problem v3.0 - expanded (pre-processed) form
description: The same problem with each worker's workable time stated explicitly instead of implied. Where the declarative form says 'this worker has a 7h contract, these buckets exist, and this cell says EQUALS:10:00-14:00', this form says 'on 2025-10-03 this worker may take A12 or A31, and nothing else'. That is the model's set of possible daily working assignments [H_wd], and the timeslots each covers is [delta_wdht] -- both defined by MathematicalDefinition7 and stored by no earlier schema. Produced by transformer/transform.py. Everything except the workable-time representation carries over unchanged: contracts, employees, demand, calendar, constraints and optimization still constrain this form. Standalone: this file does not reference any other schema.

generatedFrom.description: Provenance of this expansion. Advisory only.

assignmentCatalog.description: Every distinct daily working assignment referenced by `availability`, deduplicated. An assignment is pure time coverage: it says WHEN the worker is present, not which skill they serve. Skill choice is a separate decision [y_wdts], bounded only by the worker's own skills [S_w], so one assignment can be shared by workers of different teams.

intervals.description: Disjoint, ascending clock intervals covered by this assignment. More than one expresses a split shift (07:30-14:00 plus 18:15-21:15). Boundaries must land on the timeGrid.

endMin.description: Exclusive end; must exceed startMin. Values at or past 1440 run beyond midnight.

weightMinutes.description: Paid/contractual minutes. Kept separate from the clock span because unpaid breaks make them differ. Contract limits check against this; coverage [delta] is computed from `intervals`.

workPeriod.description: Provenance: the demand bucket this block coincides with, when it happens to coincide with one at all. Advisory; the model does not read it.

availability.description: Per worker, per day: what may happen. One entry per employee in employees.list.

assignmentIds.description: The worker's possible daily working assignments for this date [H_wd]; each id must resolve in assignmentCatalog. Empty means the worker cannot work this day. MATERIALISATION RULE, stated in bold by MathematicalDefinition7: 'H_wd does not include assignments with timeslots t not belonging to T_d'. A candidate reaching outside the day's demanded window is excluded whole -- never trimmed to fit, which would invent an assignment the enterprise never defined.

dayOff.description: Absent = an ordinary workable day. 'preferable' [D_wk] is SOFT: the worker would rather be off but may be scheduled at a penalty (ObjectiveFunction3 minimises x'_wd), so assignmentIds stays populated. 'unavailable' [U_wk] is HARD: constraint (5) forbids any assignment, so assignmentIds must be empty. The two are also subtracted separately when deriving the per-week working-day count n_wk, so they cannot be collapsed into one flag.

unavailableReason.description: Reporting only; the model treats every unavailable day identically.

forced.description: If present, this assignment is pre-committed for this date. Must also appear in assignmentIds.

competenceLevel.description: Proficiency in a team [l_ws]. LEVEL 1 IS THE HIGHEST; larger numbers are progressively lower. A demand.priorityOrder entry naming level 1 therefore means that team's most senior workers.

timeGrid.description: Cuts the day into the timeslots the model reasons over [T]. Every interval boundary must land on this grid.

slotMinutes.description: Timeslot length. Must divide 1440 (the enum is exactly its divisors). Smaller is more precise but grows the model: 15 gives 96 slots/day, 60 gives 24.

weekStart.description: First day of the week. Defines the week partition [K, D_k] that per-week limits and the working-day count [n_wk] are counted over.

holidays.description: Public holidays. Marking a day here does NOT make anyone unavailable: it exists so the enterprise can give that day its own minimum/empiric/maximum in demand.csv. Shops open on holidays, and whether a worker is entitled to take one off is a per-employee rule (v3.1). A holiday reaches a worker's unavailable set [U_wk] only through their schedule-input cell, like any other day.

hasEve.description: Whether the preceding day counts as this holiday's eve, so it can carry its own demand. The eve's date is the holiday's date minus one day; only whether it exists needs stating.

workMinutesPerDay.description: Paid minutes per day, used when a schedule-input cell says 'A'. Minutes throughout, so 7h45 is 465.

model.description: 'team' = membership only; 'competency' = membership carries a proficiency level, where LEVEL 1 IS THE HIGHEST (see $defs/competenceLevel).

contractAssignments.description: Which contract applies over which dates. Multiple entries allowed and may be discontinuous (a seasonal worker returning), but must not overlap.

teamAssignments.description: Which teams/skills [S_w] the worker holds over which dates. Holding several teams at once is normal; two entries for the SAME team must not overlap.

demand.description: Coverage wanted. The per-date numbers live in the CSV named by dataFile; this section carries the structure they reference.

dataFile.description: Path to demand.csv, relative to this file. Columns: date,workPeriod,team,minimum,empiric,maximum,start,end -- see FORMAT.md.

teams.description: Teams. These are the skill dimension [S] for both employee models; demand is keyed on them.

workPeriods.description: The buckets demand is keyed on: a demand.csv row names one of these and states how many workers that slice of the day wants. Together they also delimit the operating window. These are NOT a menu of shifts a worker picks from -- asking for one person on an 11:00-21:00 bucket is not asking anyone to work ten hours. What a worker may actually work is a contiguous block of their contracted length, anywhere on the grid inside the operating window.

timeRange.description: An end at or before the start means the bucket crosses midnight: 22:00-06:30 spans minutes 1320-1830.

breaks.description: Breaks within this period. Unpaid ones are subtracted from the weightMinutes of an assignment that coincides exactly with it, while still occupying clock time.

priorityOrder.description: Which team/level combinations to fill first. Ordered and sparse: sort entries by `order` ascending, then the FIRST entry matching a worker's (team, level) decides their priority. A bare {team} matches any level of that team; add `level` to name one exactly. Any combination not listed sorts last, all tied -- listing is opt-in, and nothing is ever excluded from the model. This drives the objective that steers multi-skilled workers toward the combinations you care about [ObjectiveFunction2]: the solver derives the model's numeric weight [p_sl] from the matched entry's position, so no weights are authored here and there is no direction to get backwards.

order.description: Evaluation position; lower is filled first. Must be unique. Ordering follows this field, NOT array position, so entries can be stored or displayed in any arrangement -- grouped by team, say -- without changing meaning. Gaps are allowed so entries can be inserted later.

level.description: Optional. Omit to match any level of this team. Remember level 1 is the HIGHEST, so {team: X, level: 1} means X's most senior, not its juniors.

rule.description: A hard rule the solver must honour. Typed: `type` is an enum and its params are schema-checked, so a mistyped rule is a validation error rather than a silently ignored no-op. Kept deliberately small -- most of what a v2.6 problem stated in constraints[] is now structural (dayOffCodes, contract limits, priorityOrder) or an objective, and only what none of those can express belongs here. Adding a type later is additive to the oneOf.

minutes.description: Minimum rest between the end of one day's work and the start of the next. The one rule the live solvers read from constraints[], and not part of MathematicalDefinition7 -- a deliberate extension.

scope.description: Reserved. v3.0 supports 'global' only; per-employee scoping is planned for v3.1. Other values are rejected rather than ignored, so a future rule cannot silently do nothing here.

constraints.description: General rules applying to everyone, and ONLY what nothing else can express. Precedence, so nothing is stated twice: structure (dayOffCodes, demandInterpretation, contract constraints, cells, priorityOrder) says what the data IS; optimization.objectives says what to optimise and its cost; constraints.hard says the rest. v2.6's soft[] and advanced[] are gone -- soft constraints were objective weights under another name, and advanced.dayOffSwapping.rules was prose no solver parsed.

boundInterpretation.description: How one algorithm phase reads one demand bound. 'hard' = must hold; 'soft' = a target entering the objective through a slack variable; 'ignore' = not read.

demandInterpretation.description: Where hard-vs-soft is decided; the demand data itself takes no position, so different phases can read the same numbers differently. The reference ILP is {minimum: soft, empiric: ignore, maximum: ignore}: its alpha_dts is the number of workers DESIRED, pursued only through the shortfall variable in ObjectiveFunction1. That model defines no hard coverage constraint and no upper bound, so empiric and maximum exist for other phases and for KPI reporting.

objectives.description: What to optimise and what each costs. The goals are exactly MathematicalDefinition7's three objective functions; an unknown goal is a validation error, not a silently dropped term.

goal.description: minimize_shortages = OF1 (minimise total under-staffing, sum of z_dts); skill_priority_weight = OF2 (minimise the priority weight of assigned team/level combinations, sum of p_sl*y', driven by demand.priorityOrder); preferable_days_off_worked = OF3 (minimise preferable days-off that get worked, sum of x'_wd).

optimization.description: One algorithm run, or a pipeline of phases. Exactly one of `algorithm` / `pipeline`.

minutes.description: Minutes from the start of the scheduling day (00:00). Values at or past 1440 express times after midnight, so a night shift 22:00-06:30 is 1320-1830 with no ambiguity.
